explainedBy: Seldon, the recorded old man in a wheelchair, stands for the dead mathematician whose timeline you must trust.

storyboard.claim: Trusting the plan means surrendering your own agency to a dead mathematician.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Seldon in his wheelchair, blank-faced and still, alone on screen.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: New point after the trust-the-timeline line: shows who you surrender to.
storyboard.addedInformation: weak: names the figure being trusted; no action shows surrender.

explainedBy: A worried man waits beside a clock: waiting for a message that cannot be opened early.

storyboard.claim: What is it like to wait for a message you cannot open early?
storyboard.concreteVisual: Pirenne slumped and worried beside a large clock icon.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Moves from the idea of trust to the felt experience of waiting.
storyboard.addedInformation: Adds the waiting posture and the clock; the vault door itself is not drawable.

explainedBy: The vault is imagined; the kept clock and the waiting man hold the scene while the door is described.
noVisual: No icon reads as a vault door (the door icon reads as a closed book).

storyboard.claim: Imagine a heavy steel vault door embedded in bedrock.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Same waiting man and clock; the callout names the steel vault.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Same stage; only the callout changes to name the vault.
storyboard.addedInformation: weak: the door cannot be drawn.

explainedBy: The timer counts down and nothing can speed it up or slow it down: the clock is the subject.

storyboard.claim: A digital timer counts down exactly 50 years and nothing can change its pace.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Clock icon kept, the man now afraid under it.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Same stage; his face turns to fear as the timer is named.
storyboard.addedInformation: The clock carries the countdown; the face adds the pressure.

explainedBy: The people outside the vault panic as the numbers shrink: two waiting men under the same clock.

storyboard.claim: The people standing outside the vault sweat and panic as the numbers shrink.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Pirenne afraid and Hardin worried standing under the clock icon.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Same stage; a second waiting person joins, both uneasy.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows more than one person panicking under the timer.

explainedBy: Outside, the situation deteriorates while they wait for the zero second: same people, same clock, war named.

storyboard.claim: Politics deteriorate and war looms while they wait for the door to open.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Hardin worried in front, Pirenne afraid behind, clock still counting.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Same stage; the callout adds the looming war.
storyboard.addedInformation: weak: war itself cannot be drawn; the callout carries it.

explainedBy: The trustees sit calmly in denial of the Anacreon threat while the mayor watches uneasily.

storyboard.claim: The board sits around a table in total denial of the Anacreonian threat.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Pirenne seated with a smug smirk, Hardin beside him worried.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Moves from the clock metaphor to the actual board room.
storyboard.addedInformation: Contrasts a complacent trustee with a worried Hardin.

explainedBy: Hardin stands and yells at the trustees; Pirenne recoils.

storyboard.claim: Salvor Hardin stands up, fists balled, and yells at them.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Hardin angry and pointing at Pirenne, who looks startled.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Same room; Hardin now acts on the trustee.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the confrontation between accuser and accused.

explainedBy: Hardin accuses the trustee of a diseased dependence on Seldon; the trustee does not react.

storyboard.claim: Relying on the vault is a diseased attitude and a conditioned reflex.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Hardin angry, pointing at the blank-faced Pirenne.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Same confrontation; the callout names the accusation, Pirenne goes blank.
storyboard.addedInformation: Pirenne blank shows the accusation is not heard.

explainedBy: Hardin says worship of the past and of authority is a stagnation that will destroy them.

storyboard.claim: Worship of the past and reliance on authority is a stagnation that will destroy them.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Same confrontation: Hardin pointing, Pirenne blank.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Same stage; the callout names what Hardin condemns.
storyboard.addedInformation: weak: repeats the accusation with a new label.

explainedBy: The narration builds a cause: the crisis is designed to trap you and squeeze off your options.

storyboard.claim: The crisis itself is engineered to be the solution and trap you.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A flow diagram: SELDON CRISIS leading to OPTIONS SQUEEZED.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Switches from the room to the structure of the trap.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows cause and effect: crisis squeezes options.

explainedBy: The same chain gains its result: only one logical move remains.

storyboard.claim: The crisis squeezes off all options until only one logical move is left.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The flow gains a third label, ONE MOVE LEFT.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Same diagram; one new label draws in.
storyboard.addedInformation: Completes the chain from crisis to a single forced move.

explainedBy: Seldon, as a recording, tells the trustees to their faces they had no freedom of action; Hardin hears it.

storyboard.claim: Seldon's recording tells them they were maneuvered until they had no freedom of action.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Seldon speaking, Hardin stunned beside him.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: New: the vault opens and Seldon speaks.
storyboard.addedInformation: Puts the speaker and his listener on screen.

explainedBy: The math forced them into a bottleneck.
noVisual: No icon in the vocabulary shows a bottleneck.

storyboard.claim: The math dictated they would be forced into this exact bottleneck.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Text only: the callout on an empty frame.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Continues the same point and promises a new detail.
storyboard.addedInformation: weak: text-carried.

explainedBy: Seldon ensured Terminus had no psychologists, to the listener's surprise.

storyboard.claim: Seldon ensured there were no psychologists on Terminus except one man.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Seldon smirking as he explains, Hardin surprised.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: New detail of the setup.
storyboard.addedInformation: The surprised reaction marks the detail as unexpected.

explainedBy: Alurin taught only rudimentary concepts and trained no successor: a thin book of knowledge.

storyboard.claim: Alurin taught only basic concepts and never trained a successor.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Seldon talking beside a book icon.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Elaborates the one exception.
storyboard.addedInformation: The book icon stands for the thin teaching.

explainedBy: The population was kept blind to the science of its own behavior: a blank-faced Hardin beside the book.

storyboard.claim: Seldon blinded Terminus to psychohistory so they would act differently than if they knew it.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Hardin blank and idle next to the book icon.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Same book; the person is blank to show ignorance.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows an uninformed population via a blank face.

explainedBy: If they knew the math they would engineer solutions, adding conscious variables that break the equations.

storyboard.claim: If they knew how the math worked they might engineer a solution, adding too many conscious variables.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A flow diagram: THEY KNOW THE MATH leading to TOO MANY VARIABLES.
storyboard.onScreenText: THEY KNOW THE MATH / TOO MANY VARIABLES
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Moves from the fact of blindness to its reason.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows why the blindness was needed.

explainedBy: The host doubts an earlier claim.
noVisual: A turn of the conversation has no visible event.

storyboard.claim: This makes me question something we discussed earlier.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Hardin worried and bowed.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Turns from the math to a doubt.
storyboard.addedInformation: weak: a mood and a transition.

explainedBy: Hardin was praised for solving the crisis with the nuclear religion before the vault opened; the smirk marks his reputation.

storyboard.claim: Earlier praise of Hardin as brilliant for using the nuclear religion.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Hardin smirking, proud.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Recalls the earlier praise.
storyboard.addedInformation: weak: reputation shown by a proud face.

explainedBy: The question of his genius is put to Hardin.

storyboard.claim: Was Hardin really a genius?
storyboard.concreteVisual: Hardin surprised mid-sentence.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Poses the question the previous beat set up.
storyboard.addedInformation: weak: face and callout carry the question.

explainedBy: If the crisis allows one action only, Hardin was no genius: a blank, ordinary man.

storyboard.claim: If only one course of action is possible, Hardin was not a genius.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Hardin blank and ordinary.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Same man; his face changes from proud to empty.
storyboard.addedInformation: The blank face removes the genius.

explainedBy: He was just the man nearest to the lever when the room shook.
noVisual: No icon shows a lever or a shaking room.

storyboard.claim: Hardin was just the guy standing closest to the lever when the walls shook.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Hardin afraid, standing alone.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Same man; the face becomes afraid as the room shakes.
storyboard.addedInformation: weak: the lever is imagined.

callout.text: Someone else would have done it

explainedBy: If Hardin were gone someone else would have done the same: a second man takes the same role.

storyboard.claim: If Hardin had been hit by a bus, someone else would have done the same thing.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Pirenne in front as the stand-in, Hardin blank behind him.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Introduces a replacement for Hardin.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows interchangeability with a second man.

explainedBy: Hardin thought he was the ultimate rebel: a triumphant pose.

storyboard.claim: Hardin thought he was the ultimate rebel.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Hardin triumphant with a smirk.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Responds to the sobering point with Hardin's self-image.
storyboard.addedInformation: His self-image is shown as triumph.

explainedBy: He rebelled against the encyclopedicists, the board and Seldon's silence: he points at the opposing side.

storyboard.claim: He rebelled against the encyclopedicists, the trustees and Seldon's silence.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Hardin angry pointing at a worried Pirenne.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Lists his rebellions.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows rebellion as an act toward another person.

explainedBy: His rebellion was exactly what Seldon calculated: the recorded planner smirks while Hardin acts unaware.

storyboard.claim: His pragmatism was what Seldon calculated; he acted flawlessly inside a script he could not see.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Seldon smirking in front, Hardin blank behind him.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Contrasts the planner and the player.
storyboard.addedInformation: Relation of planner and unaware actor.

explainedBy: Time passing wears religion out: an hourglass.

storyboard.claim: As decades pass the script must evolve because religion has a shelf life.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Hourglass icon with the callout.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Moves from Hardin to decades later.
storyboard.addedInformation: The hourglass shows time passing.

explainedBy: Neighbouring rulers refuse the priests: the envoy bars the way while the Foundation man is turned away.

storyboard.claim: Kings say no priests are allowed on their planets and the Foundation's weapon is neutralized.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The envoy angry with a halting hand, Hardin worried.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Shows the refusal.
storyboard.addedInformation: One side refusing, the other turned away.

explainedBy: A spectrum marker moves from church to marketplace as the strategy shifts.

storyboard.claim: They pivot from the church to the marketplace, a fundamental shift in strategy.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A spectrum with poles CHURCH and MARKETPLACE and the marker toward the marketplace.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: New direction after the refusal.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the pivot as movement between two poles.

explainedBy: A ruler faces the man who supplies his machines: two people, the question of who rules.

storyboard.claim: Who rules a region: the king or the one who supplies the machines it depends on?
storyboard.concreteVisual: The proud envoy and Hardin face to face.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Poses the question using the two men.
storyboard.addedInformation: Two figures stand for king and supplier.

explainedBy: A worthless heap of scrap iron on a stone floor.
noVisual: No icon shows a pile of iron buckles.

storyboard.claim: Picture a pile of crude iron buckles on a stone floor, worthless scrap.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Text only on an empty frame.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Starts an example for the shift.
storyboard.addedInformation: weak: text-carried.
